intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

experiences.name: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market where you can taste local cheeses, olives, cured meats, spices, and fresh produce alongside locals. A guided or self-guided walk through the stalls offers an authentic culinary immersion away from the heat.

experiences.name: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach
experiences.description: Visit the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon and evening when temperatures drop. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy sunbeds, and watch the spectacular Athenian Riviera sunset. Easily accessible from central Athens and close to quality seafood restaurants.

experiences.name: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine
experiences.description: Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district, learning to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and tzatziki from scratch. Classes run in the evening to avoid heat, and you enjoy your creations as dinner afterward.

experiences.name: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island
experiences.description: Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak heat. Swim at the calm, clear beaches near Aegina Town, try the island's famous pistachio products and fresh fish at a harbor taverna, and return by evening ferry. A full island experience within budget and close to Athens.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from below. Grab a cheap souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk to fuel your first night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) from an airport kiosk for €1–2
meals.lunch: Snack at the airport or on arrival — grab a tyropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the metro for €1.50
meals.dinner: Souvlaki pita wrap from a street vendor in Monastiraki (€2.50–3.50) — try Kostas or Thanasis near the square

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Buy an Ath.ena reloadable transit card at the airport metro station to save money on public transport throughout your Athens stay. Exchange a small amount of cash if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket costs around €20 but covers multiple sites — worth every cent. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for free browsing and local color.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and street art. Enjoy a sit-down meal at a local taverna with house wine.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a nearby bakery or supermarket (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and a cold Mythos beer from a bakery near the Agora (€4–5 total)
meals.dinner: Moussaka or gemista (stuffed tomatoes) at a Psiri taverna — look for daily specials boards (€8–12 with a glass of house wine)

day_by_day.notes: The combined Acropolis ticket (€20) covers 7 archaeological sites valid for 5 days — keep it safe. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Acropolis hill can be slippery.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free National Garden of Athens for a peaceful morning walk. Then explore Syntagma Square and watch the Evzone guards change at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier (on the hour). Walk up Lycabettus Hill for panoramic city views — free and rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the colorful Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian quarter with independent cafes, bookshops, and street murals. Visit the Athens Polytechnic for its impressive architecture. Browse the local street market if it's running.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Monastiraki for sunset views of the Acropolis from the rooftop bars. Opt for a cheap drink at a rooftop bar with a view rather than a full meal there.

meals.breakfast: Freddo espresso and a bougatsa (custard pastry) at a local kafeneio (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Gyros plate at a local grill in Exarchia — generous portions for €5–7
meals.dinner: Fasolada (bean soup) and bread at a traditional ouzeri in Psiri or Monastiraki (€6–9)

day_by_day.notes: Lycabettus Hill can be reached on foot via a steep path or by funicular (€7 return) — the walk is free and takes about 20–25 minutes. Exarchia is safe during the day and early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early KTEL bus or train from Athens to Nafplio (approximately 2–2.5 hours, ~€13). Nafplio is one of Greece's most charming coastal towns. Drop bags at your budget guesthouse and explore the old town's Venetian architecture and narrow lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb the 999 steps up to the Palamidi Fortress for stunning views over the Argolic Gulf (€8 entry). Alternatively, take a short boat trip to the tiny Bourtzi island fortress in the harbor (€5 return, seasonal). Cool off with a swim at Arvanitia beach, a small rocky beach just below the old town walls — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Nafplio waterfront promenade at sunset. Enjoy fresh seafood at a harbourside taverna — look for the catch-of-the-day specials.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri and coffee before the bus at Athens bus terminal (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or a gyros wrap from a grill near the Nafplio bus station (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and a Greek salad at a waterfront taverna in Nafplio (€12–15 total)

day_by_day.notes: Book KTEL bus tickets in advance online or at the Athens Kifissos terminal. Nafplio is very walkable. Arvanitia beach is a 10-minute walk from the old town and is free — bring your own towel and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient site of Epidaurus (30 km from Nafplio, reachable by KTEL bus ~€3 each way). Explore the remarkably preserved ancient theatre — one of the best in the world — and the sanctuary of Asclepius. Entry ~€12.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at Karathona Beach — a long sandy beach about 3 km from the old town, reachable by local bus or a 40-minute walk. Swim, relax, and soak up the sun. Beach entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nafplio's Syntagma Square in the evening. Try local mezedes (small plates) at a traditional ouzeri with a carafe of ouzo or local wine.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey from a small shop in Nafplio old town (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch — buy bread, olives, local cheese (graviera), and tomatoes from the Nafplio market (€4–5 total)
meals.dinner: Mezedes spread — tzatziki, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, and pita at an ouzeri (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: The Epidaurus theatre has near-perfect acoustics — drop a coin in the center and hear it from the top row. Check if there's an evening performance at the Epidaurus Festival (June–August) — tickets from €15 and a magical experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Nafplio to Athens by KTEL bus, then connect to Piraeus port. Take the ferry to Hydra island (approximately 1.5–2 hours by Flying Dolphin hydrofoil, ~€28–32 each way). Hydra is famously car-free — only donkeys and boats. Check into a budget room or small pension.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hydra Town on foot — the beautiful stone mansions, the harbor, and the hilltop cannons. Hike or rent a water taxi to one of the island's rocky coves for a swim. Spilia and Vlychos are popular free swimming spots reachable on foot or by donkey.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the harbor with a cold Alfa beer. Hydra is slightly pricier than the mainland — choose tavernas one street back from the waterfront for better value.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a Piraeus port cafe before the ferry (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Cheese pie and water from a bakery in Hydra Town (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Fresh fish of the day at a back-street taverna in Hydra Town (€12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Hydra has no ATMs that always work reliably — bring enough cash from Athens. No motorized vehicles means it's wonderfully peaceful. Water taxis are the main way to reach beaches (€5–10 per trip). Walking to Vlychos takes about 40 minutes and is free.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim at a quiet cove near Hydra Town before the day-trippers arrive. Hike up to the Monastery of Profitis Ilias for panoramic island views — free entry, about a 1-hour uphill walk. Bring water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the hydrofoil to Spetses island (about 30 minutes from Hydra, ~€12). Spetses has more beaches and a slightly more relaxed vibe. Rent a bicycle (€5–8/day) or take a horse-drawn carriage to explore the island. Head to Agia Paraskevi or Agia Marina beach for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Spetses Town (Dapia harbor area). Stay overnight in Spetses at a budget guesthouse to save on ferry costs.

meals.breakfast: Fruit, bread, and local honey from a small Hydra shop (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines and village salad at a simple fish taverna in Spetses (€8–10)
meals.dinner: Pasta with seafood or stuffed peppers at a Spetses taverna (€9–12)

day_by_day.notes: Spetses also restricts most private cars — bicycles and scooters are the main transport. The island is known for its almond sweets (amygdalota) — buy a small bag as a treat (€3–4). Check ferry schedules in advance as they can be limited.

day_by_day.morning: Morning swim at one of Spetses' best beaches — Zogeria or Agia Paraskevi (reachable by bicycle or water taxi). Crystal-clear water and pine-backed shores. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry back to Piraeus (approximately 2.5–3 hours, ~€25–30). Travel from Piraeus to Athens city center by Metro (Line 1, ~€1.40). Rest and freshen up at your Athens accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Thissio neighborhood — a trendy area with outdoor cafes facing the Acropolis. Great for people-watching and an evening coffee or beer.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri and freddo cappuccino from a Spetses bakery (€3)
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — bring your own food (bread, cheese, fruit) to save money (€3–4 self-catered)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki plate with tzatziki and pita at a Thissio grill restaurant (€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules from Spetses to Piraeus vary — book the morning departure to arrive in Athens with enough afternoon time. The Piraeus to Athens Metro is the cheapest and fastest option (avoid taxis from Piraeus which can be expensive).

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or train from Athens to Thessaloniki (approximately 5–6 hours by intercity train, ~€20–25 — book in advance on trainose.gr). Arrive in Greece's vibrant second city. Check into a budget hostel in the city center near the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Thessaloniki's famous waterfront promenade (Nikis Avenue) and the iconic White Tower (entry €4). Walk through the Ladadika district — a historic neighborhood of old warehouses now filled with cafes and tavernas. Visit the Rotunda (free exterior viewing).
day_by_day.evening: Thessaloniki is famous for its food scene — arguably the best in Greece. Head to the Modiano or Kapani covered markets for an evening food exploration.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tiropita from a bakery near Athens train station before departure (€3)
meals.lunch: Bougatsa (cream-filled pastry) from Thessaloniki's famous Bougatsa Bantis or Giannis — a local institution (€2.50–3)
meals.dinner: Grilled meats and local sausages (loukaniko) at a Ladadika taverna (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki is a food lover's paradise — it's known for its bougatsa, trigona (cream pastries), and exceptional street food. The city is very walkable. Book train tickets in advance for the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Archaeological Museum of Thessaloniki (€8) — one of the best in Greece, housing treasures from the Macedonian kingdom including gold artifacts from Vergina. Then walk up to the Upper Town (Ano Poli) — a preserved Ottoman-era neighborhood with Byzantine walls and great city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Byzantine churches of Thessaloniki — Agios Dimitrios (the city's patron saint basilica) and Agia Sofia are free or low-cost to enter. Walk along the seafront to the Aristotelous Square — the city's grand central plaza.
day_by_day.evening: Join the locals for the traditional Thessaloniki evening volta (stroll) along the waterfront. Try the local specialty — a cold Macedonian beer with a plate of meze at a seafront bar.

meals.breakfast: Trigona Panoramatos (cream-filled pastry triangles) from a local pastry shop — a Thessaloniki must (€1.50–2 each)
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki from a local grill in Ano Poli (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Seafood mezedes — grilled calamari, shrimp saganaki, and taramosalata at a Ladadika ouzeri (€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki's Upper Town (Ano Poli) requires some uphill walking but is very rewarding. The Byzantine walls offer free access and great photo opportunities. Many Byzantine churches are free to enter — dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Vergina (ancient Aigai) — the royal burial site of the Macedonian kings including Philip II, father of Alexander the Great. Take a KTEL bus from Thessaloniki (~1.5 hours, ~€5 each way). The Royal Tombs Museum is built inside the actual burial mounds — entry €12 and absolutely worth it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Thessaloniki by early afternoon. Visit the Thessaloniki street market near Kapani for fresh produce, local cheeses, olives, and spices. Pick up some local products as edible souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Thessaloniki — splurge slightly on a proper sit-down dinner at a traditional Macedonian restaurant. Try local specialties like pastourma (cured meat) or kavourmas.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita and coffee from a bakery near the bus station (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the Kapani market — olives, bread, local cheese, and fruit (€5 total)
meals.dinner: Full Macedonian dinner — grilled meats, local wine, and dessert at a traditional restaurant (€15–18)

day_by_day.notes: The Vergina Royal Tombs are one of the most significant archaeological discoveries of the 20th century — don't miss them. Photography inside the museum is restricted. Check KTEL bus times in advance as service can be limited.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Thessaloniki back to Athens by intercity train (book in advance, ~€20–25, approximately 5 hours). Alternatively, take a budget domestic flight if prices are comparable (check Aegean or Sky Express). Arrive in Athens by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use your remaining Acropolis combined ticket (if still valid from Day 2) to visit the Kerameikos archaeological site — the ancient cemetery of Athens, peaceful and often uncrowded. Alternatively, visit the free Benaki Museum garden or browse the Monastiraki flea market for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — head to the Koukaki neighborhood south of the Acropolis for a local, non-touristy dinner experience. This residential area has excellent tavernas popular with Athenians.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at Thessaloniki train station before departure (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Snack on the train — bring your own food from a Thessaloniki bakery (€4–5 self-catered)
meals.dinner: Slow-cooked lamb kleftiko or stifado (beef stew) at a Koukaki neighborhood taverna (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: If flying back to Athens, book domestic flights well in advance for the best prices (Aegean Airlines often has sales). The train is more scenic and budget-friendly. Koukaki is a 10-minute walk from the Acropolis Metro station.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — visit the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) near Omonia Square for a vivid, authentic Greek market experience. Browse the fish, meat, and spice stalls. Pick up vacuum-packed Greek coffee, dried herbs, or local honey as affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit the Acropolis Museum (€10) if you haven't already — it houses original sculptures from the Parthenon and is world-class. Or take a final stroll through Plaka and enjoy a last Greek coffee at a shaded kafeneio.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Syntagma or Monastiraki (€9, approximately 40 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — freddo espresso and a fresh koulouri with sesame from a street vendor (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki wrap or gyros from your favorite Monastiraki spot (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or snack before departure — budget €8–12 for airport food

day_by_day.notes: Keep Metro ticket to the airport handy — the express Metro (Line 3) runs every 30 minutes to the airport. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Double-check your flight time and terminal. Pack any liquid food items (olive oil, honey) in checked luggage to avoid confiscation at security.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day – no morning activities scheduled. Flight lands at 14:50.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos), clear customs and collect luggage. Take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens (~40 min). Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll through Monastiraki Square and the surrounding streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for your first taste of Athens nightlife and local food culture. Explore the lively tavernas and mezedopoleio (meze restaurants) along Miaouli and Agion Anargyron streets. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner with Greek wine.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or a quick souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk near your hotel (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional taverna in Psiri – try grilled octopus, tzatziki, and horiatiki salad (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after the 14:50 arrival. Keep the evening light to recover from travel. Exchange some cash or use ATMs in the airport arrivals hall for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a classic Greek breakfast at a local café near your hotel – freddo espresso, tiropita (cheese pie), and fresh orange juice. Then visit the Acropolis early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the midday heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and the stunning panoramic views over Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) to see the original sculptures and artifacts from the hill. Afterward, wander through the charming Plaka neighborhood – Athens' oldest district – browsing artisan shops and soaking in the neoclassical architecture. Stop at Hadrian's Arch and the Temple of Olympian Zeus nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Metro or a short taxi to Piraeus and enjoy the featured experience: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor. Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna sampling fresh grilled fish, shrimp saganaki, and local Assyrtiko white wine while watching the yachts in the picturesque harbor.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel – tiropita, freddo espresso (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Plaka – stuffed vine leaves, Greek salad, and pita at a shaded taverna (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor, Piraeus – fresh catch of the day, meze, and wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online in advance to skip queues. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip for the marble pathways. Mikrolimano is about 30 min from central Athens by Metro (Line 1 to Piraeus, then short taxi).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street – a vibrant, authentic market with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local produce. A fantastic sensory experience and great for picking up local snacks. Then explore the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market for vintage finds and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Glyfada (southern Athens Riviera) for your first beach afternoon of the trip. Glyfada Beach offers clean waters, sunbeds, and a relaxed atmosphere. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the 23°C Mediterranean warmth. The beach is easily accessible and has good facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens and dine in the Koukaki neighborhood – a local favorite with authentic, non-touristy restaurants. Try a mezedopoleio for a spread of small dishes shared at the table.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread, olives, and local cheese from the Central Market stalls (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Glyfada – grilled corn, fresh fruit, or a light sandwich (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio in Koukaki – shared plates of taramosalata, grilled halloumi, loukaniko sausage, and local draft beer (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera beaches are reachable by tram from Syntagma Square. Glyfada is about 45 min by tram. Bring sunscreen – UV index is high in June even at 23°C.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens early by ferry from Piraeus Port to Mykonos (approximately 4.5–5 hours by conventional ferry or 2.5 hours by high-speed). Book tickets in advance. Enjoy the sea crossing with coffee and a snack on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Mykonos Town (Chora). Check in to your mid-range hotel or guesthouse. Explore the iconic whitewashed alleys of Chora, visit the famous windmills at Kato Mili, and stroll along Little Venice waterfront. Browse the boutique shops and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Mykonos Town at a local taverna away from the main tourist strip – ask locals for recommendations. The area around the old port has more authentic and affordable options than the main square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Piraeus port before boarding (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Light meal on the ferry or grab a gyros wrap upon arrival in Mykonos Town (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna in Mykonos Chora – fresh fish, Greek salad, and local wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets at least a week in advance in June – routes fill up quickly. High-speed ferries (SeaJets, Golden Star) are faster but pricier. Conventional ferries (Blue Star) are more budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short bus or taxi to Agios Sostis Beach – one of Mykonos' most beautiful and less commercialized beaches. Crystal-clear turquoise water, golden sand, and a relaxed vibe. Swim and snorkel in the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Move on to Ornos Beach or Platis Gialos Beach (both accessible by bus) for more swimming and sunbathing. These beaches have good facilities, sunbed rentals, and beach bars. Enjoy the warm Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for sunset at Little Venice – one of the most iconic sunset spots in Greece. Watch the sun dip into the Aegean from a waterfront café. Then enjoy dinner at a local fish taverna near the old port.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery – spanakopita and Greek yogurt with honey (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Platis Gialos – grilled calamari, village salad, and cold Mythos beer (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Fish taverna near Mykonos old port – grilled sea bream, tzatziki, and house wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos public buses (KTEL) are affordable and connect most beaches. Buy a day pass for convenience. Agios Sostis has no facilities so bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat excursion to the sacred island of Delos (30 min from Mykonos Town, boats depart 9:00–10:00 AM). Explore one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece – the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Walk among ancient temples, mosaics, and the famous Terrace of the Lions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at Elia Beach – the longest beach on the island, with calm waters and a more relaxed crowd. Rent a sunbed and enjoy the afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Mykonos Town's famous nightlife scene at your own pace. Start with cocktails at a rooftop bar, then enjoy a final dinner in Chora before an early night ahead of tomorrow's travel.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the Delos boat – Greek yogurt, honey, and walnuts at a café (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on Delos (no restaurants on the island) or quick bite upon return to Mykonos Town (€6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Mykonos Chora – lamb chops, roasted vegetables, and local Cycladic wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Delos entry fee is €12. Boats depart from the old port and return by 3:00 PM. Bring water, a hat, and sunscreen – there is no shade on Delos. Book the boat ticket the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Mykonos accommodation. Take a high-speed ferry from Mykonos to Santorini (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing. Arrive in Santorini (Athinios Port) and transfer to your hotel in Fira or Imerovigli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into your Santorini accommodation. Take the cable car or walk the famous zigzag path up to Fira Town. Explore the main town – browse the clifftop shops, visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (€6), and enjoy the dramatic caldera views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a short bus to Oia village for the world-famous Santorini sunset. Arrive at least an hour early to secure a good viewing spot. After sunset, enjoy dinner in Oia or take the bus back to Fira for more affordable dining options.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Mykonos port café before boarding (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Fira after check-in – gyros or a café sandwich with caldera views (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira (more affordable than Oia) – moussaka, stuffed tomatoes, and local Vinsanto wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Santorini ferry tickets should be booked in advance. The cable car in Fira costs €6 one way. Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset in June – arrive by 7:00 PM for the best spots.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri – a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC (entry €12). Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Afterward, head to the nearby Red Beach – one of Santorini's most dramatic and unique beaches with striking red volcanic cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the island's southeastern coast – long black sand beaches with clear water, beach bars, and sunbed rentals. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on the distinctive volcanic black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira for dinner. Explore the caldera-side restaurants and bars. Try a local winery for a tasting of Santorini's unique Assyrtiko white wine before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery in Fira – tiropita, fresh juice, and coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perivolos – fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold beer (€15–20)
meals.dinner: Caldera-view restaurant in Fira – grilled octopus, fava dip (Santorini specialty), and Assyrtiko wine (€25–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach requires a short walk over rocky terrain – wear sturdy sandals. Buses connect Fira to Akrotiri and Perissa regularly. Santorini's fava (yellow split pea purée) is a local specialty not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning catamaran sailing tour around the Santorini caldera (typically 5–6 hours, €60–90 per person). Sail past the volcanic islands of Nea Kameni and Palea Kameni, swim in the hot springs, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, and enjoy a BBQ lunch on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: The catamaran tour typically returns by early-to-mid afternoon. Rest at your hotel or explore Imerovigli – a quieter clifftop village between Fira and Oia with stunning caldera views and fewer crowds than Oia.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely final evening in Santorini. Visit a local wine bar for a tasting of Nykteri and Vinsanto wines, then have a relaxed dinner in Fira.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early catamaran departure (€6–9 if not included)
meals.lunch: BBQ lunch included on the catamaran – grilled meats, salads, and drinks
meals.dinner: Wine bar and dinner in Fira – cheese platter, local sausages, and a glass of Vinsanto dessert wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran tour at least 2–3 days in advance through your hotel or a local agency. Bring a towel, sunscreen, and a light layer for the sea breeze. Tours typically depart from Vlychada or Ammoudi Bay.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Santorini accommodation. Take a ferry back to Athens (Piraeus) – approximately 5–8 hours by conventional ferry or 4.5 hours by high-speed. Enjoy the scenic return journey across the Aegean. Alternatively, take a short domestic flight (30 min) if budget allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Athens. Check in to your hotel. Take a relaxed afternoon walk through the Thissio neighborhood – a trendy area with café-lined streets and views of the Acropolis. Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10) if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in the Thissio or Gazi neighborhood – both are lively areas with excellent mid-range restaurants and a local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Santorini port café before boarding (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Ferry snack bar or packed food from a Santorini bakery (€6–10)
meals.dinner: Modern Greek cuisine restaurant in Gazi – creative takes on traditional dishes, local craft beer (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If taking the conventional ferry, book a comfortable seat or cabin for the longer journey. The Gazi neighborhood is Athens' creative hub with excellent food and a vibrant evening atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Cape Sounion (about 70 km from Athens). Join a guided tour or take the KTEL bus from Pedion Areos. Visit the magnificent Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60 meters above the sea – one of Greece's most dramatic ancient sites with sweeping Aegean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at one of the Athenian Riviera beaches – Vouliagmeni Lake (a natural thermal lake with mineral-rich waters, €8 entry) or Vouliagmeni Beach for a swim. The water is calm and clear along this stretch of coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens for a final evening in the city. Visit the Syntagma Square area to watch the Evzone guards at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, then enjoy dinner in the Kolonaki neighborhood – Athens' upscale but accessible dining district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or neighborhood café – Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo cappuccino (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Taverna near Cape Sounion – fresh seafood and salad with a view (€15–20)
meals.dinner: Kolonaki restaurant – slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, roasted potatoes, and a carafe of house wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Cape Sounion depart from Pedion Areos Park (near Areos Park Metro stop) roughly every hour. The round trip takes about 3 hours total travel time. Entry to the Temple of Poseidon is €10.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum of Athens (€12) – one of the world's great museums, housing treasures from across ancient Greece including the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold masks, and stunning classical sculptures. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Benaki Museum (€9) or the Museum of Cycladic Art (€7) for more curated Greek cultural experiences. Afterward, take a final stroll through the Ermou Street shopping area and the Monastiraki neighborhood for last-minute souvenir shopping and browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Athens with Acropolis views – a memorable way to end the trip. Splurge slightly on this final dinner for a truly Greek experience.

meals.breakfast: Neighborhood café near hotel – spanakopita, Greek coffee, and fresh orange juice (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a family-run taverna in Exarchia neighborhood near the National Museum – daily specials, home-cooked style (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant with Acropolis view in Monastiraki or Thissio – grilled lamb, mezedes spread, and Greek wine (€30–40 per person, a worthy splurge)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays – check the schedule. Book the rooftop farewell dinner in advance as these restaurants fill up quickly in June. Pack your bags tonight for an early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café. Depending on your departure time, take a final walk through Monastiraki or sit at a café in Syntagma Square for one last Greek coffee and people-watching. Pick up any final souvenirs – local honey, olive oil, or Mastiha liqueur make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) via Metro Line 3 from Syntagma or Monastiraki (€9, approximately 40 min). Check in for your return Air Serbia flight. Browse the airport's duty-free for Greek products.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of Greek beaches, ancient history, island-hopping, and incredible local food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast – bougatsa (custard-filled pastry), Greek coffee, and fresh juice at a local café (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a final souvlaki wrap near the hotel before heading to the airport (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Metro journey and airport check-in/security. Metro Line 3 runs directly to the airport from central Athens. Keep your transit card or buy a single airport ticket (€9). Ensure all souvenirs with liquids are in checked luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

experiences.name: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market where you can taste local cheeses, olives, cured meats, spices, and fresh produce alongside locals. A guided or self-guided walk through the stalls offers an authentic culinary immersion away from the heat.

experiences.name: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach
experiences.description: Visit the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon and evening when temperatures drop. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy sunbeds, and watch the spectacular Athenian Riviera sunset. Easily accessible from central Athens and close to quality seafood restaurants.

experiences.name: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine
experiences.description: Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district, learning to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and tzatziki from scratch. Classes run in the evening to avoid heat, and you enjoy your creations as dinner afterward.

experiences.name: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island
experiences.description: Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak heat. Swim at the calm, clear beaches near Aegina Town, try the island's famous pistachio products and fresh fish at a harbor taverna, and return by evening ferry. A full island experience within budget and close to Athens.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your hotel in the Athens/Piraeus area. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor — Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus. Sample freshly caught seafood, grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes paired with crisp Assyrtiko white wine while watching the boats sway in the harbor at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at Athens Airport arrivals hall — try a café or bistro airside
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a premium waterfront taverna in Mikrolimano Harbor, Piraeus — expect whole grilled fish, lobster pasta, and local wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Mikrolimano is only 10–15 minutes from central Piraeus and is ideal for a relaxed first evening. Jet lag tip: stay up until at least 22:00 local time to adjust quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour — Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market bursting with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local cheeses. A knowledgeable guide will walk you through the stalls, introduce you to vendors, and offer tastings of cured meats, honey, and regional specialties. A fascinating sensory immersion into Athenian daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Monastiraki and Plaka neighborhoods. Browse high-end boutiques and artisan shops, visit the Roman Agora, and enjoy the atmospheric cobblestone streets. Stop at a traditional kafeneion for Greek coffee and loukoumades (honey doughnuts).
day_by_day.evening: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine — Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as spanakopita, moussaka, tzatziki, and baklava under the guidance of a professional Greek chef. Enjoy the meal you've cooked together with wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — fresh pastries, Greek yogurt with thyme honey, seasonal fruit, eggs, and cold cuts
meals.lunch: Mezedes lunch at a premium taverna in Monastiraki — try grilled halloumi, taramasalata, and lamb chops
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner of dishes prepared during the cooking class, paired with curated Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Central Market tour is best experienced in the morning when the market is most active. Book the cooking class in advance as small-group spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon early in the morning to beat the crowds and the midday heat. Hire a private licensed guide for an in-depth historical narrative. Follow with a visit to the world-class Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach — Head to the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon. Rent a premium sun lounger and umbrella, swim in the crystal-clear Saronic Gulf waters, and enjoy the sophisticated beach club atmosphere. The water temperature in June is perfect — around 22–24°C.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a fine-dining restaurant in Glyfada or Vouliagmeni — the Athens Riviera's most elegant dining strip. Enjoy contemporary Greek cuisine with panoramic sea views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Acropolis Museum café with views of the Parthenon — salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at a sea-view restaurant on the Athens Riviera — grilled lobster, fresh fish carpaccio, and local Nemea red wine

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online in advance to skip queues. Vouliagmeni Beach has paid parking and is easily reached by taxi or private car (about 25 minutes from central Athens).

day_by_day.morning: Late morning leisure at the hotel — enjoy the pool, spa, or a slow breakfast. Alternatively, take a morning walk along the Piraeus coastal promenade (Akti Themistokleous) for fresh sea air and views of the Saronic Gulf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island — Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak tourist crowds. Explore the charming port town, visit the famous pistachio stalls (Aegina is Greece's pistachio capital), and stroll along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner on Aegina island at a harbourfront fish taverna before taking the evening ferry back to Piraeus. Enjoy grilled sea bass, prawn saganaki, and local rosé wine as the sun sets over the Saronic Gulf.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Piraeus near the ferry terminal — fresh seafood pasta and Greek salad
meals.dinner: Harbourfront dinner on Aegina — whole grilled fish, seafood risotto, and local Aegina wine

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Piraeus to Aegina run frequently and take about 40 minutes (hydrofoil) or 70 minutes (conventional ferry). Book return tickets in advance. Bring a light jacket for the evening ferry ride.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion — hire a private driver and visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff overlooking the Aegean Sea. The drive along the coastal road is spectacular. Arrive early to explore the ruins in comfort before the tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at one of the secluded coves along the Attica coast on the return journey — Legrena or Anavissos beaches offer calm, clear waters ideal for a private swim. Bring a picnic or stop at a local beach taverna.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens for a refined dinner in the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood — one of Athens' most elegant dining districts, known for its sophisticated restaurants and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start recommended
meals.lunch: Seaside lunch at a taverna near Cape Sounion or a packed gourmet picnic prepared by the hotel
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Kolonaki — contemporary Greek tasting menu with wine pairing at a Michelin-recommended restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Cape Sounion is approximately 70 km from Athens (about 1.5 hours by car). A private driver makes the experience far more comfortable and flexible than a group tour.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a high-speed ferry to Santorini. Morning departure recommended to maximize your first afternoon on the island. Check in to a luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli with caldera views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — wander the blue-domed churches, whitewashed alleys, and art galleries. Visit the Venetian castle ruins and browse premium jewelry and ceramics boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from Oia's famous castle viewpoint (arrive early to secure a good spot) followed by a romantic dinner at a caldera-view restaurant in Oia or Fira.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Oia upon arrival — fresh tomato salad, fava dip, and local Santorini wine
meals.dinner: Premium caldera-view dinner in Oia — grilled octopus, Santorini fava, white eggplant, and Assyrtiko wine from a local winery

day_by_day.notes: Book your Santorini luxury hotel well in advance — June is peak season. Oia's sunset is world-famous; arrive at the viewpoint at least 45 minutes early. Santorini's Assyrtiko wine is a must-try.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tour of Santorini's volcanic vineyards — visit 2–3 boutique wineries (Santo Wines, Domaine Sigalas, or Hatzidakis) for guided tastings of Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto dessert wine. The volcanic soil produces uniquely mineral-driven wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption of 1600 BC, often called the 'Greek Pompeii.' Hire a private guide for context and depth.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni-style experience on Santorini — visit the upscale Red Beach or Perivolos Beach in the late afternoon for a swim, then enjoy cocktails at a premium beach club as the sky turns golden.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with caldera views
meals.lunch: Winery lunch — cheese and charcuterie boards paired with local wines at one of the vineyard estates
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Fira or Firostefani — fresh catch of the day, lobster spaghetti, and local wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private wine tour in advance. Akrotiri requires a separate entrance ticket. Red Beach is a short walk from Akrotiri — combine both in one afternoon excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing trip around Santorini — depart from Vlychada or Ammoudi Bay for a half-day luxury sailing experience. Swim in the hot springs near the volcanic islet of Nea Kameni, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, and enjoy the dramatic caldera from the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a leisurely afternoon — enjoy the infinity pool, spa treatments, or simply relax on your private terrace with caldera views and a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner on Santorini at one of the island's top fine-dining establishments — a multi-course tasting menu celebrating the best of Cycladic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Onboard the catamaran — fresh Greek salad, grilled meats, seafood, and chilled wine served on deck
meals.dinner: Premium tasting menu dinner at a top Santorini restaurant — expect dishes like sea urchin, Santorini tomato soup, and slow-cooked lamb

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran charters offer a far more exclusive experience than group tours. Book well in advance. Sunset catamaran options are also available if preferred for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a high-speed ferry to Mykonos. Check in to a luxury boutique hotel in Mykonos Town (Chora) or a clifftop property with sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mykonos Town — wander through the iconic Little Venice waterfront, the famous windmills, and the labyrinthine whitewashed alleys. Browse high-end fashion boutiques and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Little Venice — enjoy fresh seafood and cocktails with views of the windmills and the Aegean sunset.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure from Santorini
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Mykonos Town upon arrival — Greek salad, fresh bread, and local cheese
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a Little Venice waterfront restaurant — lobster, grilled fish, and local Cycladic wine

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos Town is best explored on foot. The narrow alleys are intentionally confusing — embrace getting lost. June is busy; book restaurants in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the sacred island of Delos — take a short boat from Mykonos Town to this UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site, one of the most important in the ancient Greek world. Hire a private guide to explore the ruins of temples, mosaics, and the famous Terrace of the Lions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and spend the afternoon at one of the island's premium beach clubs — Nammos at Psarou Beach or Scorpios at Paraga offer luxury sun loungers, crystal-clear water, and world-class service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Mykonos Town followed by dinner at a premium restaurant — Mykonos has some of the Aegean's finest dining.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start for Delos
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Delos archaeological site café or a packed gourmet lunch from the hotel
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Mykonos Town — contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with fresh local ingredients and an extensive Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port of Mykonos Town. The site is open until 15:00 — plan accordingly. Psarou Beach is considered one of the most glamorous beaches in Greece.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast, a swim at your hotel pool, or a yoga session. Alternatively, explore the quieter northern beaches of Mykonos (Agios Sostis or Panormos) for a more secluded swimming experience away from the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private food and culture walking tour of Mykonos Town — visit local bakeries for fresh loukoumades and tiropita, sample local kopanisti cheese (a spicy Cycladic specialty), and learn about the island's culinary traditions with a local food guide.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Mykonos — enjoy cocktails at a sunset bar overlooking the windmills, then a premium farewell dinner at one of the island's celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Mezedes lunch at a traditional ouzeri in Mykonos Town — grilled sardines, taramasalata, and ouzo
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at a top Mykonos restaurant — grilled whole fish, seafood pasta, and local Cycladic wine

day_by_day.notes: Agios Sostis Beach has no beach clubs or facilities — bring your own supplies for a truly secluded experience. Kopanisti cheese is a protected designation of origin product unique to Mykonos.

day_by_day.morning: Fly back to Athens from Mykonos (short 30–40 minute flight). Check back in to your Athens hotel or a different luxury property for the final night. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Athens — revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore somewhere new. Consider the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) or a leisurely walk through the upscale Kolonaki district with its designer boutiques and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner in Athens — choose one of the city's finest restaurants for a celebratory multi-course meal. Consider a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views for a truly memorable final evening in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure from Mykonos
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a Kolonaki restaurant — modern Greek cuisine, fresh salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a top Athens restaurant with Acropolis views — tasting menu with wine pairing, ending with loukoumades and Greek dessert wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner well in advance — rooftop restaurants with Acropolis views are extremely popular in June. Consider a post-dinner walk through the illuminated Plaka district for a magical final memory.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Depending on your departure time, take a final stroll through Plaka or along the Panathenaic Stadium. Pick up last-minute gifts — premium Greek olive oil, thyme honey, saffron from Kozani, or local wines make excellent souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Athens International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the flavors, warmth, and memories of 13 extraordinary days in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast — savor every bite of Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a final quick bite at a café near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Athens Airport has a good selection of shops for last-minute Greek food souvenirs airside. Confirm your return flight details and arrange private airport transfer the evening before to avoid any morning stress.
